featured_reviews.name: Aniruddha Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hotel Saibini Gomantak is a true gem for anyone who loves authentic, flavorful food. The highlight of the menu is undoubtedly their thalis, each one packed with rich malvani taste and generous portions.

The Chicken Thali stands out with its perfectly spiced gravy, tender pieces of chicken, and a balanced combination of sides that make every bite satisfying. The Mutton Thali is equally impressive—slow-cooked mutton that is juicy, aromatic, and full of depth, making it a must-try for meat lovers. If you enjoy seafood, the Prawns Thali is exceptional, featuring fresh prawns cooked to perfection in a delicious, coastal-style curry that brings out traditional flavors beautifully.

The overall experience is enhanced by the homely touch in the cooking, quick service, and consistent quality. Hotel Saibini Gomantak is definitely a go-to place if you’re craving hearty, delicious thalis that truly capture the essence of local konkan cuisine.

featured_reviews.name: Sonam Karani
featured_reviews.review_text:
We’re both huge seafood lovers, so visiting this place was a must—and it truly felt like a paradise for seafood enthusiasts. We arrived during peak lunch hours and ordered our favorites: Bombil Fry as a starter, followed by Surmai fish Goan curry with steamed rice.

The staff was polite, attentive, and ensured our food arrived quickly. Everything was served fresh, hot, and absolutely delicious. The flavors were spot on, and the quality really stood out.

Highly recommend this place to anyone who enjoys great seafood—definitely a 5-star experience!

featured_reviews.name: Pratik B.
featured_reviews.review_text:
Right after the Malabar Elevated Nature Trail, I visited Kamla Nehru Park just above it, and it was a perfect continuation of a calm and refreshing morning.

The park offers beautiful panoramic views of the city and feels far more peaceful compared to busier seaside spots like Marine Lines. It is the kind of place where you can simply sit, feel the sea breeze, and take in the surroundings without any rush.

Morning time here has a very local, grounded feel. People come for walks, light workouts, and yoga, so it is important to be respectful of the space. Keeping noise low and avoiding littering really helps maintain the calm atmosphere for everyone.

The park is well maintained with plenty of trees, flowering plants, and shaded corners that add to its charm. One of the highlights is the lotus blooming pond, which adds a quiet, meditative touch to the landscape. You also have the well known shoe shaped structure for children, a small kids’ play area, and peaceful spots where you may notice birds and small wildlife depending on the time of day.

A very important practical point for visitors is access. This entire area is best reached only by public transport. There is no parking available and strict police barricades and check posts are in place, so street parking is not an option at all. Planning your commute in advance makes the visit much smoother.

Overall, it is a peaceful green pocket above the city with lovely sea views and a relaxing atmosphere. Best experienced early in the morning, especially between 6 am and 8 am when it is cool, fresh, and not crowded even in summer season.

featured_reviews.name: Ramya Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kamla Nehru Park, situated atop Malabar Hill and just opposite the famous Hanging Garden, is an absolute gem. Compared to other gardens, it feels perfectly maintained and peaceful. The park has well-kept paths, good security, and thoughtfully designed spots like the Eco Point and Parrot Spot. From these viewpoints, you can enjoy breathtaking views of the ocean.

The garden is an absolute nostalgia for many. The garden is very spacious. The surrounding is clean and green, the walking space is very good. It overlooks the Girgaon Chowpatty.

How to reach?
1. Get down at CST
2. Take bus no.103 and get down right outside this park

featured_reviews.name: Shankar Singh Rajput
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kamla Nehru Park is a pleasant and relaxed spot, especially popular with families and children. The big boot structure—locally known as “Mhatārīchā Boot”—is the main attraction and always a hit with kids. It’s one of those old-school charms that still brings smiles.
The garden has a large open area for walking, and you’ll notice several old, well-grown trees, which give the place a mature and calm feel. It’s nice for a slow stroll or just sitting around without any rush.
That said, the garden needs improvement when it comes to flowers. Adding more varieties of flowering plants would greatly enhance its beauty and make it more attractive for tourists and photography lovers. Right now, it feels more functional than visually exciting.
Entry is free for everyone, which is a big plus. There’s no waiting time, making it an easy stop for a casual outing. Snack sellers are available outside the park, but it’s wise to check food hygiene before eating, as quality can vary.
Overall:
A good place for a short outing, especially with children. Spacious, calm, and budget-friendly. With better landscaping and more flowers, Kamla Nehru Park has the potential to become an even stronger attraction at Malabar Hill.

featured_reviews.review_text: Kamala Nehru Park is a truly beautiful spot, and the best part is it’s free to enter. I visited on January 1st with my family in the evening, and it was absolutely charming. There are plenty of areas for children to play, and the scenery is just mesmerizing. The views over Mumbai and the ocean are really beautiful. I definitely enjoyed it a lot.

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Perched atop the verdant crest of Malabar Hill, Kamla Nehru Park serves as a sophisticated sanctuary, offering an aesthetic counterpoint to the adjacent Hanging Gardens. While the latter is celebrated for its structured topiary, Kamla Nehru Park captivates through a seamless synthesis of panoramic grandeur and rhythmic natural topography.
The park’s primary allure lies in its unrivaled vantage points. From its expansive promenades, one is treated to an elegant, sweeping vista of the Queen’s Necklace, where the urban sprawl of Mumbai meets the Arabian Sea in a breathtaking maritime embrace. The visual clarity and elevation provide a perspective that is both humbling and exhilarating, making it a premier destination for those seeking contemplative stillness amidst the city's kinetic energy.
Beyond the scenic overlooks, the park ingeniously incorporates a micro-trekking forest trail. This winding path offers a brief yet immersive escapade into dense foliage, mimicking a wilderness experience within the heart of a metropolis. The interplay of dappled sunlight and the rugged charm of the short track provides a sensory delight for nature enthusiasts. Whether you are marveling at the iconic "Old Woman's Shoe" or navigating the shaded forest enclaves, the park excels in delivering a refined outdoor experience. It remains a quintessential landmark where elegance and adventure harmoniously coexist…😍

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kamla Nehru Park, situated atop Malabar Hill and just opposite the famous Hanging Garden, is an absolute gem. Compared to other gardens, it feels perfectly maintained and peaceful. The park has well-kept paths, good security, and thoughtfully designed spots like the Eco Point and Parrot Spot. From these viewpoints, you can enjoy breathtaking views of the ocean.

One of my childhood attractions, Mahataricha boot (Old Ladies Shoes), is also there, and I specially visited to relive that memory. Unfortunately, it’s restricted to kids under 12, which was a bit disappointing.

Despite that, the park is well maintained, with clean surroundings and proper seating arrangements, making it perfect for a morning walk or a relaxing outing with close ones. Peaceful, scenic, and nostalgic—it’s definitely a must-visit spot in South Bombay.

featured_reviews.name: TripperHD Vlogs
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Koli Statue in Mahim West, Mumbai, is a significant tribute to the Koli community, the original inhabitants of Mumbai, who have played a vital role in shaping the city's history and culture. This statue is located near Mahim beach, an area traditionally inhabited by the Koli fishermen. The Koli community's fishing activities have been central to Mumbai's economy for centuries, and their influence can still be seen today in various coastal areas.

The statue is a symbol of the Koli people's contribution to the city, representing their hard work and resilience. It depicts a Koli fisherman in traditional attire, often seen with a fishing net or tools that highlight their deep connection to the sea. The statue not only honors their livelihood but also serves as a reminder of the cultural diversity that Mumbai prides itself on.

Mahim West, where the statue is located, is a neighborhood steeped in history, with landmarks such as the Mahim Fort and Mahim Church nearby. Visitors to the area often find the Koli Statue a point of interest, providing insights into the lesser-known yet significant cultural heritage of Mumbai's fishing community.

featured_reviews.name: Tasmiya Shiledar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahim Fort, located in the Mahim area of Mumbai, is one of the lesser-known historical sites in the city. Built by the Portuguese in the 16th century, it originally served as a strategic military outpost. However, over time, the fort fell into disrepair and now exists in a somewhat dilapidated state, making it less of a tourist attraction compared to other forts in Mumbai like Gateway of India or Bandra Fort.

### Key Aspects:
1. **Historical Significance**: The fort was originally constructed by the Portuguese in 1680 to defend the area from the Marathas. It was later taken over by the British in the 18th century. It’s interesting from a historical standpoint, though not much of the original structure remains intact.

2. **Location**: Mahim Fort is located near the Mahim Beach, which is a busy part of Mumbai. The fort itself is tucked away in a residential area, which means it’s not a prominent tourist spot and can sometimes be overlooked.

3. **Condition**: The fort is in poor condition and lacks proper maintenance. Most of the fort’s structure is reduced to ruins, and it’s surrounded by modern buildings. It doesn't offer the same panoramic views or grandeur as other forts, which can make it less appealing to those looking for a more scenic or fully preserved historical experience.

4. **Accessibility**: The fort is accessible to the public, but you’ll likely need to search for it amidst local streets and residential buildings. It’s not as well-marked as other historical sites in Mumbai, so visiting may require a little bit of patience and exploration.

5. **Cultural Context**: While the fort itself may not be a major draw for tourists, the area around it offers a glimpse into the local life of Mumbai, with its mix of residential homes and bustling markets. It’s a good place to experience the contrast between Mumbai's rich history and its modern-day hustle and bustle.

### Overall Review:
Mahim Fort can be an interesting visit for history buffs or those looking to explore off-the-beaten-path locations in Mumbai. However, if you're expecting a well-preserved, tourist-friendly fort, you might be disappointed. It's a quiet spot, perfect for those looking for a peaceful break from the busy city, but it's not a must-see if you're short on time.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahim Fort is the oldest fort in Mumbai. Connecting the east-west coasts of Mumbai and guarding the bay of Mahim, this fort was known as the gatekeeper of the waterway. At the mouth of the Mahikavati aka Mahim bay, which separates the islands of Mumbai from the mainland, Pratap Bimba Raja built the Mahim fort in 1140 AD and established his capital there. And by calling people doing various types of business, trade, enterprise, science And the seeds of culture were planted on the island of Mumbai.
After the fort came under the control of the British, the English architect Jerrold Augier rebuilt the existing fort. In 1672 AD, the Portuguese attacked the fort of Mahim. At that time the fort was equipped with 100 soldiers and 30 guns; So the Portuguese could not conquer it. Then on 14 February 1689 Siddhi Yakut Khan of Janjira attacked Mumbai with 2500 soldiers. At that time, after conquering the fort of Mahim, he ravaged the area for a year, looting
Protected by strong fortifications and bastions on all sides, the entrance of this fort stands as a testimony of British architecture. The crafts on it and the raised pillars on both sides can be seen. Due to encroachment in the fort, nothing else can be seen.
Mahim fort on the sea can be reached in 10 minutes if you get off at Mahim (West) station on the Western Railway and walk towards Mahim beach along Mori Road.

Tried their cheese garlic poie and it was super loaded and cheesy — definitely a must-have. The golden fry chicken with peri peri fries was crispy and full of flavour, perfect if you’re in the mood for something indulgent.

My personal favourite was the squid dry with neera dosa — soft, well-cooked and really flavourful. Also loved the cheesy peri peri fries, proper comfort food vibes.

Had a blue lagoon on the side which was refreshing and went well with everything.

Overall, great food, nice vibe, and totally worth visiting if you’re around Bandra. Would definitely come back!

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is owned by the same people who run fresh catch, so it wasn't a surprise that the food here was good too.  We tried the kurkuri prawns which are served with peri fries. The prawns were alright, nothing special, they tasted good because of the banger dip. Fries were lovely though.
The prawns poi was top class, the staff recommended it so we went for it. It's tasty and filling. The poi broke apart too quickly as if it was old bread but there was no noticeable  taste difference. It was still damn good. Can't wait to go here again to try their other options.

featured_reviews.name: Xavier Dsouza
featured_reviews.review_text: Amazing Place to eat fries! The fries and chicken were top notch amazing Taste and the tiramisu Frappe was amazing too everything here was fantastic. The vibe, The staff and aesthetic everything was top tier.Worth a Try!!!!!!!

featured_reviews.name: Omkar Verma (ShotsbyOmkar)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Frys with Fries is shaking up Mumbai's food scene as the first seafood fast-food chain in the city. With a friendly owner, boneless dishes for convenience, and impeccable freshness, this spot is a game-changer.🤌

We tried-
*Bang Bang Mushroom*, a treat for mushroom lovers with its unique flavors and generous portion size. 🤌❤️*The Fish Stuffed Poie, a Goan bread specialty, was super tasty—well-cooked, boneless, and satisfying in quantity. *The Chicken Xacutti paired with Poie* showcased the classic Xacutti gravy's rich and superb taste.🤤❤️ Crunchy Coco Shrimp also stood out with its delightful crispiness and touch of coconut sweetness, and the refreshing Blue Lagoon Mojito tied it all together.🍹

Ambiance was also decent, worth visitingg with friends/ family for some gooood boneless food.

Key Highlight:-

1. Most of the food  in priced below 400
2.  Interative staff
3. Open till 1 am.
4. Frehly cooked Boneless.me.

Do visit this place with your loved ones ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Manali Mayekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Mahim Koliwada Seafood Plaza run by Koli Bachatgat Mahila and had such a lovely experience! They offer so many varieties of seafood dishes with authentic koli flavours. All the women here are so kind, friendly and welcoming ❤️

We ordered tandoori prawns, crab lollipop, khekada masala and tandalachi bhakri. The crab lollipop was super crunchy and fresh, and the khekada masala with bhakri was absolutely delicious 😋 The bhakri paired perfectly with the rich and spicy gravy.

The only reason I’m giving 4 stars for food is because the tandoori prawns, which we ordered first as soon as we reached, were served at the very end. But honestly, the prawns were worth the wait — juicy, fresh and perfectly cooked. 12 pcs cost around ₹500.

They also have stalls for chicken items, soda drinks and desserts, so there’s a lot to try here. Overall, it was a great experience. You can enjoy your dinner beside the sea with a beautiful view of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link 🌊✨

featured_reviews.name: Mandar Sukhathankar
featured_reviews.review_text: I have been visiting Matsyagandha , the last stall on the other end from the entrance. The ladies are exceptionally hospitable and took care of the needs of our entire group and paid special attention to children. Must haves....kombdi vade, surmai fry , bombil fry and surprisingly well made real chicken lollipop without the extra globules of corn starch that has come to be the hallmark of all "chinese" items these days. The lollipop served here was all meat and flavor ,no atta binding. Will love to visit again for amazing sea breeze and vista.

featured_reviews.name: Kalpesh Kandalgaonkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahim Seafood Plaza is a paradise for seafood lovers. The seafood served here is extremely fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. From classic coastal dishes to rich seafood curries, every item reflects authentic taste and quality.
The ambiance is comfortable, the service is prompt, and the staff is courteous. One big advantage is the availability of parking, which makes the visit hassle-free.
If you enjoy fresh, delicious seafood with great taste and convenience, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended for true seafood enthusiasts!

featured_reviews.name: Ganesh Badgeri
featured_reviews.review_text: Mahim Koliwada Seafood Plaza is a good spot for seafood lovers. Tried bombil fry, clam masala, bhakari, solkadi, and chicken Koliwada - all were tasty. Food was spicy, but quantity was good. Proper seating area and parking space available. Best part is the view of Bandra Worli Sea Link. Overall, worth a visit for seafood cravings.

featured_reviews.name: Ritesh Shirolkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
What an amazing place...We just loved the place and planning to visit again.
Fish was very tasty, marinated in koli masala.
Few suggestion
1) It is open on Wednesday, Friday, Saturday & Sunday.
2) Either go before 7:30pm or after 10pm , because the rush is heavy between 8pm to 10pm.
There are around 8 to 9 koli mahila bachat gut stall , Visit every place ask the price and seat accordingly based upon your pocket.
3) Getting sea face seat is a marathon..lol
